content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Recovering Lost Commits with git reflog"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Git's 'reflog' is a powerful mechanism for recovering lost commits. It records updates to the tip of branches and other references, allowing you to go back in time even if you haven't committed or pushed your changes."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding the Reflog"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"The reflog (reference log) is a local-only mechanism. It's not pushed to remote repositories. It tracks when the tips of branches and other references were updated in the local repository. This includes commits, merges, resets, and other operations that change the state of your branches."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"Using git reflog"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"To view the reflog, use the following command:"},{"order":7,"type":"code","text":"git reflog"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"This will display a list of recent actions, along with a reference (e.g., 'HEAD@{2}') that you can use to refer to a specific state."},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Recovering a Lost Commit"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Let's say you accidentally reset your branch to an older commit and want to recover the commits that were lost. Here's how you can use the reflog:"},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Run 'git reflog' to find the commit you want to recover. Look for entries that indicate the point in time before the accidental reset."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Identify the commit hash associated with that entry (e.g., 'a1b2c3d')."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"You can then create a new branch pointing to that commit, or reset your current branch to that commit. To create a new branch:"},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"git branch recover-branch a1b2c3d"},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Alternatively, to reset your current branch (be careful, this will overwrite your current state):"},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"git reset --hard a1b2c3d"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"After creating the 'recover-branch', you can examine the recovered commits and merge them back into your main branch if needed."},{"order":18,"type":"subheading","text":"Reflog Expiry"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"The reflog entries expire after a certain period. By default, entries are kept for 90 days, and entries reachable from the current commit are kept indefinitely. You can configure these expiry times using the 'git config' command."},{"order":20,"type":"code","text":"git config gc.reflogExpire \"200 days\""},{"order":21,"type":"code","text":"git config gc.reflogExpireUnreachable \"60 days\""},{"order":22,"type":"subheading","text":"Reflog for a Specific Branch"},{"order":23,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can view the reflog for a specific branch by specifying the branch name:"},{"order":24,"type":"code","text":"git reflog show mybranch"},{"order":25,"type":"subheading","text":"Safety Considerations"},{"order":26,"type":"paragraph","text":"Using 'git reset --hard' can be destructive. Always double-check the commit hash before resetting your branch. It's generally safer to create a new branch from the reflog entry first, examine the commits, and then decide how to integrate them into your main branch."},{"order":27,"type":"paragraph","text":"The reflog is a powerful tool for recovering from mistakes, but it's essential to understand how it works and use it carefully."}]
